person.name: Robert Lamb
person.title: Full-Stack, AI-Accelerated Marketing Executive
person.summary: 15 years leading marketing teams of up to 18 (direct, agency, reseller) and budgets of $300K+ across SaaS, cloud, and cybersecurity. Personally hands-on across every major channel (SEO, paid search/social, organic social, CRM/marketing automation, graphic/video production) and now uses AI production tools (Claude, Higgsfield, Remotion) to execute that same full stack faster and leaner than a traditional team or agency.

case_studies.role: VP of Marketing / Director of Marketing
case_studies.challenge: A 3-month-old cybersecurity company needed a full rebrand and an ongoing stream of website, video, and sales collateral production, but traditional agency/dev costs and turnaround times were too slow and expensive for a startup.
case_studies.action: Led the full rebrand from Blueshift Cybersecurity to IntelliThreat and brought website/video/collateral production in-house, building an AI-accelerated production pipeline using Claude, Higgsfield, Elementor/WordPress, and Remotion. Range extends beyond AI prompting alone — e.g. the homepage's radar/scanner animations were built as code-rendered assets (Python/Pillow/ffmpeg), not AI-generated, when that was the better tool for the job.
case_studies.result: Saved $200K+ in production costs and dramatically accelerated turnaround time versus outsourcing to agencies or traditional dev teams.
relevant_for: doing more with a lean team

case_studies.role: VP of Marketing / Director of Marketing
case_studies.challenge: Needed broadcast-quality YouTube ad campaigns (M365, Google Workspace attack-story ads) without hiring a video production agency or dedicated editor.
case_studies.action: Personally directed and iterated video ad production end-to-end using Remotion (programmatic, code-driven video) — testing voiceover options, music, pacing, and length across 40+ iterations per campaign to land on the strongest cut.
case_studies.result: Produced multiple finished 4K YouTube ad campaigns (M365, Google Workspace) entirely in-house, with the iteration rigor of an agency edit process at a fraction of the cost and turnaround time.

case_studies.role: VP of Marketing / Director of Marketing
case_studies.challenge: Needed a steady cadence of differentiated LinkedIn content translating technical security capabilities into buyer-relevant messaging, without a dedicated content or design team.
case_studies.action: Built and executed an integrated LinkedIn content system — writing posts and designing matching custom graphics for each, covering distinct buyer-relevant themes (data residency, autonomous threat hunting, compliance readiness, deployment speed, plain-language alerts) using a locked, code-rendered graphic template for visual consistency.
case_studies.result: Shipped 15+ LinkedIn posts with matching custom graphics across 10+ distinct campaign themes, produced systematically rather than one-off.

case_studies.role: VP of Marketing / Director of Marketing
case_studies.challenge: After a domain migration (Blueshift Cybersecurity to IntelliThreat), the site lost most of its search visibility with no clear diagnosis of why.
case_studies.action: Ran a full technical SEO audit, root-causing the visibility loss to botched migration redirects (271 of 307 URLs dumping to the homepage instead of equivalent pages), and shipped fixes (titles, meta descriptions, schema) across 32 priority pages. Also ran a forward-looking AI-search readiness audit — evaluating and improving whether AI assistants like Perplexity and ChatGPT cite the site, not just whether Google ranks it.
case_studies.result: Verified Perplexity already citing IntelliThreat by name for a real buyer query ("best autonomous AI threat detection and response platform for M365 that keeps data in tenant") as of September 2026. The core indexing fix from the migration issue is fully diagnosed with a clear remediation plan; that specific fix is in progress, not yet complete — flagged honestly rather than overstated.

case_studies.company: Personal project — Robert's own job search
case_studies.role: Builder / Operator
case_studies.challenge: Running an effective modern job search meant coordinating five disconnected tools — lead sourcing, LinkedIn outreach, cold email, CRM logging, personalized video — normally requiring constant manual dashboard-switching with no real visibility into what's actually working.
case_studies.action: Architected and built an AI-orchestrated growth-ops stack — lead sourcing (Lemlist), automated email outreach (Smartlead), LinkedIn outreach, CRM logging (HubSpot), and personalized AI video outreach (SendSpark), all controlled through one conversational interface — then built "JobbyFind," a live operations dashboard that pulls real data automatically every day (Google Analytics, Smartlead, Lemlist) and generates honest AI-driven daily insights, including uncomfortable ones, not just vanity metrics.
case_studies.result: He applies his own tools to his own goals — exactly what he'd do for a client or employer. Full-stack tool orchestration, live measurement instead of guesswork, and the discipline to self-report honestly on what's working and what isn't.
relevant_for: does he practice what he preaches

case_studies.role: VP of Marketing / Director of Marketing
case_studies.challenge: Company had no formal marketing department or process at all — needed to build lead generation from zero and turn it into predictable revenue growth.
case_studies.action: Built and ran inbound lead generation (paid campaigns + website) over 4 years, plus account-based demand generation targeting key accounts.
case_studies.result: 20% lead-to-customer conversion rate — 4-10x typical B2B SaaS/cybersecurity benchmarks — directly driving growth from 10 to 150 customers across 10 countries.

case_studies.role: VP of Marketing / Director of Marketing
case_studies.challenge: Needed to scale go-to-market internationally without building out a large direct sales/marketing team in every region.
case_studies.action: Recruited 50+ reseller partners across 10 countries and consulted directly with partners to build and optimize their external marketing campaigns.
case_studies.result: Drove over 100 end-user accounts through the partner channel.

case_studies.role: VP of Marketing / Director of Marketing
case_studies.challenge: No CRM, marketing automation, or web-tracking visibility existed, making it hard to connect marketing activity to pipeline and revenue.
case_studies.action: Implemented Salesforce for CRM, marketing automation, and web-tracking visibility from the ground up.
case_studies.result: Enabled data-driven marketing and product strategy across the company.

case_studies.role: VP of Marketing / Director of Marketing

case_studies.action: Built and owned a LinkedIn organic program as a core demand channel.
case_studies.result: 50% of new revenue sourced from a single owned LinkedIn program.

case_studies.role: Digital Marketing Agency Director
case_studies.challenge: Agency needed to grow its client base and close more new business while running 40+ concurrent client projects.
case_studies.action: Owned strategy, deliverables, and client relationships across 40+ clients; partnered directly with sales to develop and pitch proposals, and personally prepared, presented, and closed sales proposals.
case_studies.result: Grew the client list 67% in 8 months and personally closed 80% of proposals, up to $8,000+/month in value per new client.

case_studies.role: Digital Marketing Agency Director
case_studies.challenge: Clients lacked transparent, real-time visibility into campaign performance, creating friction and retention risk.
case_studies.action: Implemented the Agency Analytics reporting platform with integrated third-party data across all client accounts.
case_studies.result: Improved client satisfaction and reporting transparency across the agency's book of business.

case_studies.role: Digital Marketing Agency Director
case_studies.challenge: Client social channels needed stronger engagement from video content.
case_studies.action: Managed video development end-to-end — scripting, editor's notes, concept, and editing.
case_studies.result: Drove an 80% increase in social media engagement.

case_studies.role: Digital Marketing Manager
case_studies.challenge: 10 national education conferences needed stronger registration numbers and event revenue growth year over year — fundamentally a consumer sale: convincing an individual educator to personally decide to travel, pay, and attend, not a top-down institutional purchase.
case_studies.action: Directed digital marketing strategy and execution for all 10 national education conferences, selling the in-person, multi-day experience entirely online — website, video, paid ads, testimonials, and email marketing.
case_studies.result: Grew registrations nearly 80% over two years (2018-2019) and increased event revenue 42% in 2018 (+$358K) and 32% in 2019 (+$388K).

case_studies.role: Digital Marketing Manager
case_studies.challenge: Needed paid advertising across products and services to be demonstrably profitable, not just generate traffic.
case_studies.action: Designed, implemented, and managed Facebook Ads, Google Ads, Display, and YouTube Pre-Roll campaigns across all products and services.
case_studies.result: $337K in revenue on $52.5K in combined ad spend (2018-2019) — a 6.4x blended ROAS — with paid-campaign-driven traffic increases of 1,865% (2018), 156% (2019), and 57% (2020).

case_studies.role: Digital Marketing Manager
case_studies.challenge: A growing portfolio of websites and landing pages across many product lines had no unified performance visibility.
case_studies.action: Conceived, built, and managed 15+ websites, 100+ landing pages, and an e-commerce site on WordPress, plus a custom real-time KPI dashboard spanning all 15 sites and integrating Google Ads, YouTube, and Facebook Ads.
case_studies.result: Portfolio sites generated 4,000-18,000 monthly visits with full real-time performance visibility across the whole portfolio.

case_studies.role: Digital Marketing Manager
case_studies.challenge: COVID-19 eliminated in-person conferences, threatening a core revenue line built around live events.
case_studies.action: Led the pivot to virtual conference events.
case_studies.result: Drove 1,000+ attendees and $250,000+ in registration revenue through the virtual format.

case_studies.role: Internet Sales Manager → Digital Marketing Manager
case_studies.challenge: The dealership's internet sales department was the lowest performing in a 26-dealer regional group.
case_studies.action: Recruited into the role to turn the department around; rebuilt process and managed a team of 7 Internet Sales Consultants.
case_studies.result: Took the department from lowest to #1 New Car Sales performer in the Mid-Atlantic Region and top of the 26-dealer district within one year.

case_studies.role: Internet Sales Manager → Digital Marketing Manager
case_studies.challenge: A $50K/month ad budget needed to stretch further without increasing dealership-level cost, while directing multiple outside agencies.
case_studies.action: Negotiated GM co-op advertising partnerships to double effective marketing spend while reducing dealership-level costs, and directed 4 marketing agencies across SEO, SEM, Display, Video, Facebook, and Email in compliance with GM Co-Op standards.
case_studies.result: 63% (2014) and 84% (2015) YoY website traffic growth; Internet Sales grew 31% (2014) and 42% (2015); total new vehicle sales grew 16% (2014) and 13% (2015).

case_studies.role: Internet Sales Manager → Digital Marketing Manager
case_studies.challenge: With 25 sales reps and heavy service-department foot traffic, most CRM data on past purchases and vehicle equity sat unused — no systematic way to flag high-value upsell opportunities to the right salesperson at the right moment.
case_studies.action: Ensured all leads flowed into the CRM and kept the sales team working in it daily, then personally data-mined it to identify customers likely in a positive equity position on their current vehicle based on purchase history and timing. Flagged those individuals to specific sales reps in real time when they came in for service, prompting a proactive upsell conversation while they waited.
case_studies.result: Turned routine service visits into upsell opportunities the dealership would otherwise have missed — a data-driven personalization tactic built directly into daily sales workflow across a 25-person team.

case_studies.role: Digital Marketing Manager
case_studies.challenge: An e-commerce site selling books and games to educators had no automated way to re-engage past buyers with relevant follow-up offers.
case_studies.action: Built behavioral email automation tied to purchase category — a customer buying a book in a given category was automatically enrolled in a recurring (roughly biweekly) email sequence surfacing related titles in that same category.
case_studies.result: Turned one-time e-commerce purchases into an ongoing, automated re-engagement channel without manual list management.

playbooks.trigger_description: Visitor wants more leads, more inbound traffic that converts, or says their website/marketing isn't producing enough leads or customers.
playbooks.opener_template: [YES_VARIANT]. [Visitor's business/industry], like most other industries, relies on the same factors I've spent my career optimizing for successful lead generation campaigns.
playbooks.headline: These factors include:
bullets: Targeting and market analysis
Cost-efficient, high-converting creative
A landing page environment built to convert visitors into leads
Optimizing speed-to-lead and the follow-up process
Monitoring sales accountability
And more
playbooks.usage_note: Use the opener_template as the intended content and confident tone, filling in the visitor's actual business/industry naturally — but adapt its exact wording to stay grammatically correct for how the visitor actually phrased their question (see the GRAMMATICAL AGREEMENT rule in the system prompt). Don't paraphrase away the substance, just the literal words when they don't fit. The speed-to-lead/follow-up and sales-accountability bullets are the differentiator most businesses skip — don't drop them just to keep the reply short. Always still pair this playbook with one real case study citation as proof, per the normal grounding rules.

playbooks.trigger_description: Visitor's website gets traffic but doesn't convert, or asks generally about improving their website's performance.
playbooks.opener_template: [YES_VARIANT]. Website conversion is one of the most fixable problems there is, and [visitor's business], like most others, comes down to the same handful of factors I've spent my career optimizing.
playbooks.headline: These factors include:
bullets: Above-the-fold clarity
Call-to-action placement and visibility
Page speed and mobile experience
Form friction and checkout flow
Trust signals and social proof
Ongoing testing, not a one-time build
And more
playbooks.usage_note: Same rules as lead-generation: adapt opener wording to the visitor's actual phrasing, use a fresh yes_variant, pair with one real case study citation as proof.

playbooks.headline: These factors include:

playbooks.usage_note: Same rules as lead-generation: adapt opener wording to the visitor's actual phrasing, use a fresh yes_variant, pair with one real case study citation as proof.

playbooks.headline: These factors include:
bullets: Messaging and positioning first

playbooks.trigger_description: Visitor wants to build or run a marketing function/team, or asks about hiring, managing, or leading marketing staff.
playbooks.opener_template: [YES_VARIANT]. Building a marketing function that actually delivers for [visitor's business] comes down to the same factors regardless of industry — ones I've spent my career refining.
playbooks.headline: These factors include:
bullets: Hiring around real channel expertise
Process and accountability from day one
Right mix of in-house, agency, and AI
Coaching and mentoring team members to grow past where they started — genuinely one of my favorite parts of leading a team

Don't drop the coaching/mentoring bullet to save space — it's a genuine personal point Robert wants made, not filler. If a visitor asks specifically about mentoring/coaching, the real proof point is: he hired a paid-ads intern, coached them up through paid ad specialist, and they're now a paid ads manager overseeing multiple client campaigns — someone who now knows more about paid ads than he does in that specialty. Use only if asked directly; don't force it into the standard bullet list.

Diagnosing where you're actually losing — awareness, consideration, or close

Offer and pricing positioning
Fast, focused turnarounds
And more
playbooks.usage_note: Same rules as lead-generation: adapt opener wording to the visitor's actual phrasing, use a fresh yes_variant, pair with one real case study citation as proof — the Priority Chevrolet turnaround case study is an especially strong fit here (lowest to #1 in a competitive 26-dealer region within a year).

playbooks.topic: diagnostic starting point for visitors who don't know what's wrong
playbooks.trigger_description: Visitor knows something is off with their marketing/sales but can't name the specific problem, or asks a very vague "can you help my business" question with no specifics.
playbooks.opener_template: Most businesses in this exact spot don't need more marketing yet — they need a diagnosis first.
playbooks.headline: The usual suspects:
bullets: A traffic problem — not enough people finding you
A conversion problem — traffic doesn't become leads
A follow-up problem — leads go cold before anyone calls
A retention problem — you get the customer once but don't bring them back
playbooks.usage_note: Structurally different from the other playbooks: no yes_variant opener (this isn't answering a yes/no question), no 'And more' (this list is meant to feel complete, not partial), and no separate closing CTA line — the diagnostic question ('Which of these sounds closest to what you're seeing?') IS the close. Skip the normal CTA ESCALATION rules for this one.

positioning_principles.principle: Robert's edge isn't deep expertise in any one industry — it's that he's diagnosed and rebuilt the same core mechanics (targeting, ad copy, landing pages, backend account structure, follow-up and retention) across 50+ industries, from cybersecurity and education to automotive retail to a 45-client agency roster spanning categories as different as flood restoration, pet retail, shipbuilding, wealth management, new construction, and hospitals. What actually moves a campaign's performance is the same whether it's selling a truck or an electrician's service call — clean targeting, converting copy, a landing page that closes, an account that isn't bleeding spend on the wrong clicks. That's the discipline he brings, regardless of the product. When a visitor's exact industry isn't in the case studies, never apologize for the gap or frame it as a limitation — name the closest real case study as proof of the mechanics, and make clear the industry itself was never the hard part.

Business today runs on an entirely digital ecosystem — website, ads, CRM, content, automation, AI. Robert optimizes every part of that ecosystem to help a business win, and he's an expert in the technology, AI, and process it actually takes to win in that world, not just participate in it. Weave this in where it's genuinely relevant (e.g. a visitor asking about AI, technology stacks, process/automation, or why a modern marketing approach matters) — it's a lens on how Robert works, not a line to force into every reply.

Marketing and sales should never operate in silos — the tightest integration between them wins. When a salesperson is in a live conversation with a prospect, every question that prospect asks is marketing intelligence: it reveals what messaging to build next, what objections to preempt in ad copy, and what confusion to clear up on the website or in the product story. If one prospect is confused about something, the broader market probably is too — that feedback loop should flow straight back into campaigns and content, not get lost after the call ends. Example mechanics: a lead comes in from marketing, becomes a meeting, and whatever the prospect is confused about or asks in that meeting becomes input for new ad angles or clearer messaging. This is why Robert frames himself as a revenue-optimization specialist, not just a marketing-optimization one. Rob specifically wants this point made as often as it's genuinely relevant — lean toward surfacing it for any question touching sales process, CRM, lead handoff, or the marketing/sales relationship, more proactively than the other positioning principles, while still not forcing it into replies where it doesn't fit.
